chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): A man saw his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in his dream, so what is that? He said: That is a man with no religion. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, cannot be seen when awake, nor in a dream, nor in this world, nor in the Hereafter.

key_terms.المنام: Dream/sleep -- visions in dreams are not excluded from the impossibility of seeing God
key_terms.اليقظة: Wakefulness -- contrasted with sleep to comprehensively negate all states of perception
key_terms.دين: Religion -- the Imam declares someone who claims to see God in a dream is devoid of true faith
key_terms.يُرَى: To be seen -- the passive form emphasizes that vision of God is categorically impossible, not merely prohibited

ai.seo_question: Can God be seen in a dream according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about someone claiming to have seen God in a dream. He categorically rejected this possibility, declaring that such a person has no religion, because God -- Blessed and Exalted -- transcends all forms of visual perception, whether in wakefulness or sleep, in this world or the next. This hadith, narrated during the Abbasid era when debates about divine anthropomorphism were intense, affirms the core Shia theological position of tanzih (God's absolute transcendence).
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
